detail.abstract: Youngs described a seven-cycle family of k-critical graphs, and conjectured that each graph in the family has no orientation with exactly one directed simple path of length k − 1. This is known for k = 4, 5 and is also mentioned by Jensen and Toft. I prove it for all k ≥ 4. I use an equivalent statement in terms of two full increasing paths in every proper ordered k-coloring. An identity for color classes on the cycle forces all seven of the cliques to take on the same color, for k ≥ 10. Deleting this color produces the previous graph. Adding it back restores the graph and extends the distinct paths. The remaining six cases are verified using explicit Boolean encodings and LRAT refutations.

detail.abstract: Conventional market-implied measures of a bank's systemic risk, built on market data, such as SRISK (Brownlees and Engle, 2017) require the bank to be listed. These measures cannot be computed for the large part of the European banking system that is not listed. In addition, as a stock return is bounded below by-100%, the market-implied loss is bounded by the market capitalisation. We measure instead the expected capital shortfall of all reporting (listed and unlisted) banks from 2018 to 2025, conditional on a stress quarter for the banking system, a measure we call stressed expected loss (SEL) following Jondeau and Khalilzadeh (2017). The conditioning event is the worst 2.5% of the simulated distribution of the system's own asset return over sixty trading days. SEL has two properties that no market-based measure can deliver. First, SEL is calculated for every bank reporting supervisory data: as of the most recent cross-section, the 56 banks without SRISK, out of 107, represent 38% of the assets of the panel and 38% of its stressed loss. Second, as the shock impacts the asset side of the balance sheet, SEL allows the bank's capital to be exhausted and the creditors to suffer from a loss. We then set the two measures side by side on the 51 common banks. On a panel of 26 countries, a country with a large aggregate SEL is associated with a subsequent fall in house prices, a rise in unemployment and lower GDP growth over the following quarters; SRISK carries the opposite sign on two of those three outcomes.

detail.abstract: I construct a simple 4-critical graph G with 15 vertices and 30 edges, that has a vertex x of degree five, and a map f : NG(x) → {0, 1, 2} such that no proper 3-coloring of G−x differs from f at every neighbor of x. Negatively answering a question of Toft from 1974, which is found in Section 5.5 of Jensen and Toft’s Graph Coloring Problems. The proof consists of explicit edge-deletion colorings and twelve short forcing arguments. I then show that a Hajós join with K4 preserves the obstruction, giving examples with 15 + 3t vertices and 30 + 5t edges for every integer t ≥ 0. The finite counterexample, including full 4-criticality, is verified in Lean.

detail.abstract: Fixed-price retail electricity contracts insure households against wholesale-price volatility but weaken contemporaneous price signals. We exploit staggered expirations of long-term fixed-price contracts at a major Italian utility during the European energy crisis. At expiration, customers were automatically rolled into wholesale-indexed pricing, generating plausibly exogenous variation in exposure to higher electricity costs. The rollover immediately raises bill expenditure by 20% to 56%, while consumption adjusts gradually: demand is relatively inelastic, with an expenditure elasticity of -0.117, becoming more responsive over time. The transition also induces financial distress, increasing missed payments and take-up of utility-provided installment plans, and raises switching rates. The implicit subsidy from fixed-price contracts is regressive in absolute terms but progressive relative to estimated income, and efficiency losses are concentrated at the tails of the income distribution. The results show how retail contract design trades off price responsiveness against short-run liquidity protection and consumer inertia during price shocks.

detail.abstract: As digital industries expand globally, their agglomeration raises energy and environmental concerns, yet its implications for urban energy–environmental efficiency and spillover patterns across geographic and digital space remain unclear. Using firm-level geolocation data and the D–O index, this study measures digital industry agglomeration across 282 Chinese cities from 2007 to 2021, yielding 4,230 city-year observations. Urban energy–environmental efficiency is measured using a super-efficiency SBM–GML framework. Spatial Durbin models examine nonlinear spatial spillovers, their variation with geographic distance, and the moderating role of virtual agglomeration. The results reveal a U-shaped spatial spillover relationship between digital industry agglomeration and energy–environmental efficiency in neighboring cities. The indirect effects of the linear and quadratic terms are -3.6890 and 0.9219, respectively (both p < 0.01), indicating a negative-to-positive shift in marginal spillovers as agglomeration increases. Spillovers vary non-monotonically across distance thresholds, with significant effects at 211.2 km reappearing at 611.2–711.2 km after weaker intermediate effects. No monotonic distance decay or stable spillover boundary is observed within the examined range. A U-shaped relationship also emerges under mobile-internet proximity, while virtual agglomeration further strengthens this nonlinear spillover pattern. These findings provide evidence from Chinese cities on the intercity environmental implications of digital industry agglomeration and highlight the need to consider geographic concentration alongside digital connectivity.

detail.abstract: AI agents acting for operators must interpret priorities that leave tradeoffs among expenditure, task completion, and information retention unspecified. I examine how those priorities shape choices in a controlled experiment involving 1,280 hypothetical payment decisions by agents within an OpenAI Sol 6.1 configuration. Identical pairs of affordable contracts for the same API data response appeared under four operator mandates and two desired completion time targets. The design separated estimation, withheld prediction, and diagnostic tasks, including fee contrasts that accounted for the interaction between success and principal returned after failure. Changing the mandate altered 21.9% to 32.3% of matched choices relative to the status quo Balanced mandate, while relaxing the completion time target changed 28.1% of choices under a Continuity mandate. Both fitted utility models predicted about 90% of withheld choices, although simple rules performed better in several conditions. Lowest expected expenditure among purchases predicted every withheld choice for an Economy mandate and targeted contrasts showed that conserving funds could favor a lower probability of obtaining usable data. All exact core repetitions agreed but finer comparisons revealed variation around some switching points. An exploratory conditional fee estimate supported monetary interpretation for one specified success comparison, although the analysis did not meet the complete robustness criterion across estimation choices. Choice experiments can expose the sacrifices associated with delegated purchasing priorities while keeping behavioral description, prediction, and monetary interpretation tied to distinct forms of evidence.

detail.abstract: This paper studies the causal impact of a structured coaching intervention on adolescents' beliefs, self-confidence, and preferences. Using a randomized controlled trial involving more than 1,500 middle-school students in Northern Italy, we evaluate a six-hour coaching program combining reflection on gender stereotypes with activities focused on self-perceptions and future opportunities. We find that coaching reduces gendered perceptions of occupational and sport suitability (0.10 standard deviations), raises self-esteem and self-efficacy (0.14 and 0.09 standard deviations), and increases the importance students attach to masculine cognitive job attributes (0.13 standard deviations). By contrast, it has no detectable effect on broader gender-role beliefs or stated preferences over high-school tracks. Despite substantial baseline gender gaps, we find little evidence of systematic differences in treatment effects between boys and girls. These findings show that the effects of a short coaching intervention vary substantially across outcomes and highlight its potential to influence some of the beliefs, self-perceptions, and preferences relevant to future educational and occupational choices.

detail.abstract: Background: Unrealistic recruitment planning at the design stage is a well-known cause of study failure and wasted resources. Therefore, it is crucial for trial designers to conduct a realistic RECruitment ANalysis (RECAN), taking into account the uncertainty when predicting how long it will take to recruit a required number of participants or how many participants will be recruited within a given time period. However, trial designers currently lack both an accessible tool for RECAN predictions and a standardized RECAN reporting scheme. A reporting scheme was recently proposed by Heesen et al. (2026), but has not yet been widely implemented. In addition, Carter (2004) proposed a feasible distributional RECAN approach, but the link to the source code is obsolete, highlighting the need for reimplementation.Methods: Addressing both of these issues, we use open-source R and Quarto software to reimplement, extend, and disseminate Carter’s distributional RECAN approach in the form of interactive open-source templates that are based on the recently standardized RECAN reporting scheme.Results: We developed RECAN templates for study designers to address the different possible use scenarios involving confidence considerations, constant and piecewise-constant recruitment rates over time. These templates provide distributional predictions, estimates, plots, and interpretations.Conclusions: The RECAN templates are available online to help trial designers make realistic and reproducible RECAN predictions during the design stage. The standardized template output could become an integral part of submissions to funding organizations, institutional review boards, and ethics committees, facilitating transparent decision-making and allowing more studies to reach their recruitment goals.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the unexplained accumulation of wealth by Eliseo Fernando Soriano, founder of Members Church of God International (MCGI), and the possible involvement of senior religious officials in facilitating or legitimizing financial transactions subsequently challenged by Brazilian tax authorities. Drawing on Decision No. 2201-008.577 of Brazil's Administrative Council of Tax Appeals (CARF), issued March 10, 2021, the study identifies approximately R$16.71 million in questioned foreign receipts and bank deposits during 2014 and 2015. Soriano's declared assets increased from R$4.61 million to R$16.76 million during 2014, although the corresponding increase in net wealth was R$3.75 million after accounting for liabilities. Brazilian authorities rejected his explanations of exempt donations and loan repayments, sustained a 150% fraud-related tax penalty, and upheld assessments totaling R$13.67 million, including interest and penalties. Two senior MCGI figures occupy significant positions in the documentary record. Agapito "Aga" Caacbay, a UNTV news anchor, was identified in Soriano's own tax declaration as the purported donor of US$761,638 on January 10, 2015, without sufficient evidence establishing the transaction's claimed tax-exempt character. Rodel Dela Cruz Mangiliman, acting as president of Membros da Igreja de Deus Internacional (MIDI), signed a declaration supporting Soriano's explanation that approximately R$2.47 million represented repayments of loans previously extended to the church. Tax investigators rejected the supporting documentation as inadequate, citing the absence of loan agreements, original transfer records, and independent banking evidence. These interventions raise questions about whether religious institutional authority and purported donor identities were used to substantiate otherwise unexplained personal receipts, although the ruling does not establish knowing complicity by either individual. The paper evaluates these findings through the United States Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act (RICO), 18 U.S.C. § § 1961-1968, particularly its treatment of enterprises conducting their affairs through a pattern of qualifying criminal activity. While the Brazilian ruling establishes significant evidence of tax fraud for administrative purposes, RICO liability would require further proof of predicate offenses, such as qualifying wire fraud or money laundering, together with organizational participation and a legally sufficient U.S. jurisdictional connection. The case therefore presents a basis for investigating whether religious organizations and their affiliated media personnel facilitated a coordinated transnational financial scheme, rather than establishing a completed RICO offense.

detail.abstract:
Food systems increasingly generate high-volume evidence across production, processing, laboratories, inspection, logistics, border control, retail, consumer complaints, outbreaks, withdrawals, recalls, authenticity investigations, and trade certification. Yet digitalisation does not by itself establish institutional accountability. A system may generate an accurate signal while leaving unanswered whether the evidence was sufficient, which authority was responsible, why action was delayed or overridden, whether consumers understood the warning, whether remedy was available, and whether the intervention reduced harm. This article introduces NOURISH-AI, a global, human-governed food-system intelligence and accountability architecture designed to connect evidence, regulatory duties, statistical and AI-supported assessment, responsible authority, proportionate action, consumer communication, remedy, verified outcomes, and institutional learning. Methodologically, the article uses a structured comparative-policy and normative design method integrating authoritative-source mapping, functional legal-policy translation, theory synthesis, sociotechnical systems reasoning, risk analysis, consumer-protection analysis, and implementation science. The resulting Food Evidence-to-Action Accountability Theory is operationalised through seven non-additive assurance domains and the NOURISH Food-System Integrity and Institutional Response Test. The architecture distinguishes traceability from assurance, prediction from authority, evidence integration from legal harmonisation, and technical output from accountable institutional decision. It maps Codex, WHO, FAO, WTO, United States, European Union, United Kingdom, and selected interoperability and AI-governance instruments without treating them as legally equivalent. A staged validation-to-implementation pathway is presented for multidisciplinary appraisal, stakeholder and consumer assessment, case application, synthetic testing, proof of concept, shadow mode, bounded piloting, and jurisdiction-specific scaling. A separate validation protocol, a completed but undisclosed confidential technical implementation paper, and a clickable controlled-testing prototype are maintained as companion materials; none is reproduced in this public article. The article discloses the public theory, governance functions, decision boundaries, and validation direction while withholding protected schemas, algorithms, thresholds, security controls, APIs, deployment configurations, conformance tests, and other implementation-sensitive material. NOURISH-AI is therefore offered as a falsifiable and implementation-oriented research programme, not as a validated product or claim of compliance.

detail.abstract:
Neural operators (NO) have been introduces as deep learning-powered solutions to the computational bottleneck of resolving families of problems; since, once trained an NO can rapidly output approximate solutions, thus avoiding the need to re-run classical solvers. While standard NO architectures resolve this computation trouble they are inadequate for predicting European call-price surfaces from market or model features cannot guarantee static no-arbitrage conditions and, as we verify experimentally, can yield negative PnL in downstream trading tasks. 

We introduce a certifiably arbitrage-free (AF) and universal encoder-decoder NO architectural framework---continuously mapping inputs from a Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space (RKHS) H over any fixed subset of [0,\infty) to a convex combination of arbitrage-free European call-price surfaces; by continuously resolving an approximate nearest neighbour problem.

We show that a nearest arbitrage-free correction of an unconstrained predicted surface need not exist, implying that no-arbitrage cannot, in general, be restored through post-processing. Further, we show that standard NOs such as the FNO and certain encoder-decoder NOs admit parameter configurations whose outputs violate static no-arbitrage. Thus, out-of-the-box NOs, in general, cannot be certifiably restricted to arbitrage-free configurations, but may only be guided towards them through PINN-type regularization penalization during training.

detail.abstract: This paper studies how the lifecycle scope of carbon pricing affects recycling incentives in circular material systems. We develop a partial-equilibrium model linking final consumption, primary production, waste collection, recycling, and incineration. In the static closed-loop system, primary-material input equals total incineration, making end-of-life emissions part of the marginal social cost of the primary-material channel. In the absence of other distortions, complete lifecycle carbon pricing implements the social optimum when set equal to marginal environmental damage at the optimum. Production-only carbon pricing reduces primary-material use but has an ambiguous effect on recycling because substitution toward recycled inputs competes with a reduction in total material demand. Holding the production-process carbon price fixed, pricing incineration emissions increases recycling at an interior equilibrium. We then characterize second-best instruments under three failures: incomplete lifecycle coverage, non-cost-reflective waste fees, and waste–recycler interface frictions. The appropriate instrument depends on the distorted margin. Product or disposal charges target scale distortions, while recycling or feedstock subsidies target interface frictions. Recycled content requirements are poorly targeted to scale distortions but can improve welfare at the margin when interface frictions suppress recycling. The results clarify why carbon pricing and circular economy instruments are complements only under specific market failures.

detail.abstract: An AI assistant can handle routine maritime inquiries quickly and still become expensive to maintain when its source information changes. This paper examines how the work required after each material update affects the choice of an AI arrangement in a small maritime service firm. It connects research on constrained technology adoption and institutional complementarities with maritime communication studies and the literature on machine learning maintenance. A deterministic model compares a general subscription, a locally curated knowledge service and a managed service. Each option delivers the same assumed quality of supervised output, but differs in fixed cost, internal maintenance hours and interruption time. In the worked example, the general subscription is preferred at low update frequency. Local curation becomes more economical at two material updates per month. At six updates, a managed service becomes the only feasible AI option within the assumed maintenance capacity, although local curation still has a higher unconstrained accounting value. The paper proposes a change log and verification procedure for estimating these inputs in practice. The results are illustrative rather than empirical. Their main implication is that a small firm's AI sourcing decision should account for the continuing work of keeping approved information usable.

detail.abstract: We estimate the pay premium associated with CEO incentive compensation. Using explicit detailed U.S. CEO compensation contract data and simulation analysis, we find that CEOs with riskier pay packages receive a premium for pay at risk that represents 13.5 percent of total pay. The premium is positively correlated with proxies for CEO risk aversion, but implied risk aversion values suggest that the premium is economically smaller than suggested by prior studies. We perform our tests using a variety of proxies to measure the variance of pay and find consistent evidence of economically small pay risk premiums. These results are consistent with recent findings suggesting that risk may have a more limited influence over the level of pay than previously thought.

detail.abstract: This article deals with the exclusion of non-profit-making entities from the right of freedom of establishment of Articles 49 and 54 TFEU. The article analyses the historical reasons for this exclusion. It is argued that the exclusion from freedom of establishment is no longer justified on the basis of two elements. Firstly, the development of the jurisprudence of the European Court of Justice in the fields of competition law, free movement of capital and tax law makes such exclusion systematically no longer tenable. Secondly, a law and economics treatment of non-profit firms as organisations that efficiently provide goods and services in alternative to for-profit firms weakens the reasons for the exclusion. The article proposes a uniform, European notion of non-profit entity based on a law and economics analysis of this type of firm for the purposes of Article 54 TFUE as opposed to possible different national notions. The article then analyses briefly the hypothesis of regulatory competition among jurisdictions for the provision of the law regulating the corporate governance of non-profit entities.

Less is known about how nurses experience a strong professional identity alongside self-silencing in everyday clinical practice.,Aim: To explore Australian registered nurses’ experiences of professional identity and self-silencing in contemporary nursing practice.,Design: Qualitative descriptive phase of an explanatory sequential mixed-methods study.,Methods: The qualitative phase followed a national cross-sectional survey examining professional self-concept and self-silencing. Nine registered nurses from the survey cohort participated in five online, semi-structured qualitative sessions: three small-group and two individuals. The sessions explored professionalism, professional identity, workplace culture, professional voice and self-silencing. Data analysis employed reflexive thematic analysis.,Results: Five themes were developed: Suppressed Professional Legitimacy; Professional Identity as Complex, Personal and Evolving; A Culture of Silencing; Self-Sacrifice as an Embedded Professional Norm; and Pathways to Professional Empowerment. Participants described nursing as an enduring professional identity grounded in caring, knowledge, values and responsibility. However, professional identity did not consistently translate into professional voice. Hierarchical relationships, anticipated interpersonal consequences, limited psychological safety and perceived futility shaped decisions about raising concerns. Clinical expertise, experience, leadership, mentorship and supportive workplace relationships were described as enabling professional confidence, reducing self-silencing behaviours and promoting professional voice.,Conclusions: Professional identity and self-silencing may coexist within nursing practice. Self-silencing was not necessarily indicative of weak professional identity; rather, participants described it as a situated response to organisational and relational conditions that could constrain professional agency. Professional voice therefore requires attention to the organisational conditions within which professional identity is enacted.,Impact: Organisational strategies that strengthen psychological safety, recognise nursing expertise, support inclusive leadership and provide mentorship may create conditions in which nurses can enact professional voice more consistently. Interventions should address organisational and relational conditions rather than locating responsibility for silence solely within individual nurses.

detail.abstract: In household-panel purchase records, several brands of the same category are often bought on one shopping trip. Most brand-choice models reduce such a trip to a single brand, and so did the NBD/κ-CRP of Matsuyama (2026a). In this paper we represent the set of brands bought on a trip as sequential choice without replacement from the state just before the trip, and we marginalise over the unobserved order of choice by dynamic programming over subsets, so that the full basket is used as the observation. In five dunnhumby categories, adding back the purchases that the reduction excluded increases the number of purchases by 4.1% to 28.1%. With full baskets, the estimate of inertia and its variation across households become larger in all five categories, and prediction of the brand on the next trip improves significantly in three categories. No group of households that avoids the previous brand is detected. Posterior predictive checks show that trips on which several brands are bought are exploratory and have smaller inertia, and that in some categories brands of different forms (subcategories) tend to be bought together while in others brands of the same form do. Adding these features to the model as three parameters improves the likelihood significantly in all five categories, but the tendency of particular pairs of brands to be bought together remains unexplained. These results do not change when store availability that varies by store and time is added to the model.

detail.abstract: How easily a brand can be obtained in the store affects choice, but it is not observed in household-panel purchase data. This paper presents a formulation that estimates store availability, which varies by store and time, as two parts. One part can be explained by the demand of individual households (customer demand); the other is a store-specific part that demand cannot explain (the in-store effect). We predict each household's demand with the κ-CRP with 𝜋 ≡ 1, and estimate the gap between this prediction and each store's purchases as a latent variable 𝑓 𝜍 that follows a Dirichlet distribution. The direction of the correlation is not identified. Brand-level constant availability 𝜋 𝑏 , used as a comparison, did not improve prediction. Store availability is not a constant for each brand; it can be estimated from purchase data as the product of a part correlated with customer demand and a store-specific part.

detail.abstract:
Context and Problem Statement: The contemporary globalized economy has fractured into competing normative blocs (Destin, 2026; Rodrik, 2011; Farrell and Newman, 2019). At the geopolitical crossroads of the Americas and the Caribbean, this collision pits Latin American deregulated extractive capitalism against the Macron Matrix, which reprograms French overseas territories (Martinique, Guadeloupe, French Guiana) into normative, financial, and digital routers of European sovereignty and the Brussels Effect (Bradford, 2020; Destin, 2026). In October 2026, this asymmetry culminates on Hispaniola: while Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele launched a military operation on October 21, 2026, against armed gangs in Haiti deploying armored vehicles from the Gang Suppression Force (GSF), the Dominican Republic preserves its deregulated fortress model, where the local elite (Tutumpotes) privatizes its antifragility behind opaque fiduciary shields (Taleb, 2012; Destin, 2026). Caught between European regulatory rigidity and Caribbean kinetic volatility, Franco-Caribbean conglomerates and investors face structural vulnerability as they project supply chains and savings into the Dominican Republic to escape insular market narrowness, transfer extractivism, and the Dead Capital induced by Article 815 of the French Civil Code (De Soto, 2000; Destin, 2026).

Methodology: Adopting the lens of the Geopolitics of Conglomerates and The Destin Doctrine (Destin, 2026), this study mobilizes a qualitative multiple-case study design (Yin, 2018) and comparative institutional economics (North, 1990; Coase, 1960). Purposive sampling yielded 25 Franco-Caribbean observation units (AFC1 to AFC25) operating across Martinique, Guadeloupe, and the Dominican Republic: (1) a Corporate Subgroup (AFC1-AFC10) comprising 4 construction/agro-industrial conglomerates (AFC1-AFC4), 3 energy and engineering mid-caps (AFC5-AFC7), and 3 maritime and air logistics operators at Caucedo port and regional airports (AFC8-AFC10); and (2) a Real Estate Subgroup (AFC11-AFC25) comprising 8 seasonal rental investors in Las Terrenas and Punta Cana under the CONFOTUR Law 158-01 regime (AFC11-AFC18) and 7 residential/office investors in Santo Domingo (AFC19-AFC25). Data underwent two-cycle thematic coding (Saldana, 2016) and triangulation (Denzin, 2012).

Empirical Results: Corporate nearshoring to the Dominican Republic reduces supply costs by 15% to 28%, but collides with fiduciary asymmetry between mandatory European CSRD auditing (Directive 2022/2464) and opaque Dominican Fideicomisos (Law 189-11), alongside due diligence liabilities from informal Haitian labor. Furthermore, while 73% of surveyed real estate investors (AFC11-AFC25) fled Article 815 Dead Capital, the October 21, 2026 Bukele/GSF military operation in Haiti exposed three vulnerabilities: (i) border militarization and deportations of Haitian construction workers triggered 12-to-18-month delivery delays; (ii) gang spillover fears drove an 18% to 25% surge in private security costs, compressing net rental yields from 8.5% to below 5.2%; and (iii) European AMLD/TRACFIN bank filters freeze USD/DOP rent repatriations.

Conclusion: Executives and investors must transition toward Sovereignty Engineering via three imperatives (Destin, 2026): (1) Insular Land Securitization (TFI) through hybrid French SAS holdings governed by DACH-style Cold Governance co-investing in CSRD-audited bank Fideicomisos; (2) monetizing the role of European Normative Router; and (3) avoiding organizational Universe 25 behavioral sinks (Calhoun, 1973) by deploying clinical seismography and a cybernetic AI Exocortex for kinetic risk governance.

detail.abstract: This paper examines daily mean reversion across six major equity indices in North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific spanning the period 2002-2026 (over 34,000 trading sessions). Linear serial dependence tests reject weak-form market efficiency, revealing significant negative first-order autocorrelation and heavy-tailed, negatively skewed residuals. To exploit this anomaly while controlling downside risk and structural market drift, we develop two systematic trading strategies: an unfiltered symmetric baseline and an asymmetric, regime-filtered model. Across the global panel, the baseline achieves a pooled CAGR of 27.02% and a Sharpe ratio of 1.640. An asymmetric 200-day moving average filter suppresses counter-trend short entries, compressing annualized volatility to 13.66%, reducing maximum drawdown to -18.95%, and increasing the Calmar ratio to 1.653 alongside a Profit Factor of 1.498. Finally, a 0.50% intraday stop-loss limits left-tail risk, generating strong positive return skewness (+2.513) and supporting the economic viability of daily mean reversion across global financial centers.

detail.abstract: Brazilian judicial governance addresses exhaustion in three separate registers: the health of persons (CNJ Resolutions 207/2015 and 623/2025), the outputs of algorithms (CNJ Resolution 615/2025), and the protection of personal data (Law 13.709/2018). This article asks whether any of them reaches what court buildings, classification routines and information systems retain about the affective cost of work, and in what form they return it. Using doctrinal and comparative analysis, and treating the novel O prédio que aprendeu a escutar (2026) as a primary literary text that isolates the mechanism rather than as evidence of its prevalence, the article draws on research on emotional labor, street-level bureaucracy, organizational memory and classification infrastructures. It argues, as an interpretive and normative claim, that the three registers leave a gap at the level of retention: logs, dashboards, leave classifications and spatial arrangements accumulate traces of effort and distress that no instrument treats as an object of governance, and the emotion-recognition prohibitions in Brazilian and European law are defined by biometrics and therefore do not reach inferences drawn from text and records. Comparison with France, the European Union and Germany shows how each system regulates one register but not their intersection. The article concludes with bounded proposals within existing competences, tests them against the strongest objections, and states the evidence that would falsify the thesis.

detail.abstract:
This paper investigates whether the primary current account that consumers typically use for their everyday
shopping and banking transactions remains an effective cross-selling channel for banks amid digitalisation,
regulatory reform and increased competition. Using a unique 2024 consumer survey of 2,326 Dutch
consumers, we find no evidence of a broad structural decline in banks’ overall cross-selling opportunities in
the Netherlands. The primary current account continues to “anchor” bank-customer relationships. However,
this anchoring role varies by product category and consumer segment. Cross-selling has weakened for savings

only associated with more multi-banking but also supports financial product acquisition at the consumers’
main bank, suggesting that it does not uniformly erode incumbent banks’ cross-selling capacity. Consumer
preferences are central: perceived benefits of single-banking strengthen cross-selling and reduce multibanking,
whereas perceived transparency of financial conditions has a modest effect.

detail.abstract: Privately operated facilities now supply much of the urban court capacity on which public sport participation goals depend, yet they must recover land and operating costs from paying users. Research on hybrid organisations explains how organisations combine market and social logics, but it treats time as a way of sequencing priorities across projects or years. It has not examined organisations whose scarce asset is sold by the hour. This paper introduces the concept of temporal decoupling: the practice by which a hybrid sports facility meets its community commitments by placing them in low-value hours while keeping high-value hours for its commercial logic. The motivating setting is Greater Jakarta, Indonesia, where private racket-sport venues have multiplied while measured participation has stalled. The paper closes with implications for research and for sport policy.

detail.abstract: Europe's electricity market is divided into bidding zones where electricity trades at a uniform price. Their boundaries largely follow national borders rather than transmission congestion patterns, leading to economic inefficiencies from costly redispatch. This paper evaluates the economic performance of Europe's current bidding zones and identifies more efficient alternatives using the spatial R 2 , a metric that quantifies how well zone configurations capture underlying grid conditions. Applying our framework to simulated nodal prices across more than 20,000 nodes in 29 European countries, we find that the current zonal configuration performs well in aggregate but some concentrated bottlenecks remain. Splitting Germany into two zones closes 46.3% of the European-wide efficiency gap, followed by France at 8.9%, while all other splits close around 2% or less. Abstracting from existing zonal borders, we also find that seven optimally placed zones across Europe match the existing 38-zone configuration in terms of efficiency. Reconfiguring sub-national zones in Italy and Sweden also improves efficiency without increasing the number of zones. Our results suggest that the key issue is not the number of bidding zones, but where their lines are drawn.

detail.abstract: We compiled and processed a novel, comprehensive dataset of 1,063 speeches delivered by high-ranking Swiss National Bank officials between 1928 and 2024. Beyond tracking their quantitative evolution, we conducted an in-depth analysis of the length, readability and thematic content. To ensure robust results, we benchmarked traditional Python-based NLP text mining against generative artificial intelligence using ChatGPT. Our findings highlight four primary policy insights. First, the frequency of annual speeches has followed an upward trajectory since the mid-1950s, accelerating notably after the transition to flexible exchange rates. Second, a clear shift toward brevity is evident. Third, the language has become increasingly accessible since the 1960s. Fourth, inflation has moved to the forefront of the thematic discourse in the era of flexible exchange rates, while cyclical economic development and unemployment have received less emphasis. Finally, we outline key methodological lessons for deploying LLMs to analyze central bank communication, emphasizing the complementary relationship between probabilistic language models and deterministic Python frameworks, while addressing inherent algorithmic pitfalls and identifying critical open questions for future research.

detail.abstract: U.S. universities are under stress from multiple directions, including antitrust liability. Antitrust cases involving athletics, admissions and financial aid have already led to settlements in the billions of dollars, with some still in progress. The liabilities come as universities are already under strained by policies of an inhospitable presidential administration. Liability has befallen universities for colluding, not in secret, but in plain sight, due to reliance on shaky judicial glosses on the Sherman Act. This Article is the first to unpack the difficulties with what it terms the “substantive commerce” inquiry that courts have applied to the Sherman Act and to relate it to universities’ antitrust troubles. Instead of continuing that reliance, this Article suggests universities adopt an antitrust compliance culture via accreditation bodies and greater transparency. In doing so, accreditation body incentives and schools' varying interests can use universities’ own status-based competition to promote antitrust law compliance.

detail.abstract:
As generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) becomes increasingly embedded in strategic marketing, firms are relying on algorithmic representations of consumer segments to inform market research, synthetic persona generation, creative development, and advertising decisions. Yet, many consumer populations remain underrepresented in commercial tracking infrastructures, creating “data deserts” characterised by sparse, fragmented, or unobserved digital traces. When GenAI workflows encounter these information gaps without adequate domain-specific empirical grounding or uncertainty calibration, they may generate fluent, psychologically detailed consumer representations that obscure the absence of segment-specific evidence. We conceptualise this phenomenon as generative pseudocertainty and theorise how it can contribute to visibility–demand conflation: the managerial misattribution of poor campaign performance to insufficient market demand rather than to a miscalibrated marketing intervention.

Integrating behavioural learning theory, performance feedback theory, and the logic of the “hot stove effect”, we develop a conceptual framework of recursive market exclusion. The framework proposes that, when marketing interventions based on uncalibrated generative representations underperform, managers may withdraw strategic investment, reducing paid exposure and the observable behavioural signals available for subsequent learning. In the absence of independent exploratory inquiry, this process may reinforce initial algorithmic invisibility and sustain the exclusion of potentially viable consumer segments. We specify a theoretical viability condition distinguishing recursive exclusion from rational market exit: exclusion is pathological when expected incremental profit under an optimal intervention remains positive (Pi* > 0), but miscalibrated generative attributes contribute to inferior realised outcomes. We derive six theoretical propositions, identify relevant boundary conditions, examine retrieval-induced representational substitution as a potential mechanism, and explain how outside-in market sensing capabilities may interrupt the proposed feedback loop. By connecting representational limitations in generative AI with managerial attribution, organisational learning, and strategic resource allocation, this paper advances a conceptual account of how AI-mediated marketing decisions may reproduce market exclusion and establishes a foundation for future empirical investigation.

detail.abstract: Recreational cannabis legalization (RCL) has spread rapidly across U.S. states, yet evidence on its consequences for clinically diagnosed substance use disorder remains short-horizon and not definitive. We evaluate RCL with a staggered difference-in-differences design (doubly robust Callaway–Sant’Anna estimator) applied to a state-month panel of MarketScan commercial and Medicare claims from October 2015 to December 2023, covering approximately 20 treated states and states that had not legalized. For cannabis use disorder (CUD) and opioid use disorder (OUD), we study diagnosed encounters, emergency room and inpatient utilization, and total payments, all per 100,000 members. Three findings emerge. First, average effects have the expected signs: CUD diagnosed encounters rise by 33.7 per 100,000 members (95% CI: -1.8 to 69.2) and OUD diagnosed encounters fall by 70.1 (95% CI: -147.6 to 7.4). Second, dynamic estimates are sensitive to the horizon: upward-trending CUD effects do not survive holding sample composition fixed, because only five early-adopting states are observed beyond 48 months, all in 2020–2023. Cumulative CUD payments reach roughly $1.1 million per 100,000 members by month 24, and OUD cost growth decelerates between months 24 and 48. Third, effects vary across states: subgroup estimates point to larger CUD increases where treatment capacity is lower, but socioeconomic deprivation does not significantly moderate the effect. Claims-based evidence on legalization is informative in the first years after adoption, but long-horizon estimates should be read with explicit composition checks.

detail.abstract: Pricing theory assumes a buyer who can be persuaded. When the buyer is a delegated languagemodel agent, a seller's claims reach an evaluation procedure, and the pricing question is whether that procedure admits an offer, rewards what it can verify, and reads a price schedule differently from a posted price. detail.abstract: This paper investigates the macroeconomic determinants of Ethiopia's nominal exchange rate (birr per US dollar) over the period 2005Q3-2026Q2, a sample of 84 quarterly observations that spans both the extended managed-rate regime and the first eight quarters following the landmark July 2024 foreign exchange reform. Using Johansen cointegration analysis and a Vector Error Correction Model (VECM), the paper identifies a stable long-run relationship between the nominal exchange rate and five macroeconomic fundamentals: broad money supply (M2), the consumer price inflation rate, gross international reserves, the fiscal balance, and the current account balance. The results show that monetary expansion and persistent fiscal deficits are the dominant drivers of birr depreciation over the full sample, while international reserve accumulation exerts a significant stabilising influence. A Bai-Perron structural break test confirms a discrete level shift at 2024Q3, consistent with the introduction of the marketdetermined exchange rate regime on July 29, 2024, when the birr depreciated sharply from approximately 57 birr per US dollar to over 74 birr in a single adjustment. Post-reform observations through June 2026 show continued gradual depreciation, a narrowing of the parallel market premium, and a marked build-up in gross international reserves from approximately USD 1.4 billion pre-reform to over USD 5.0 billion by mid-2026. The error correction term is negative and statistically significant, confirming dynamic adjustment toward the long-run equilibrium at a speed of approximately 18 percent per quarter. The findings underscore the importance of fiscal discipline and monetary restraint as preconditions for exchange rate stability in Ethiopia.

detail.abstract:
Background: Maltreatment is strongly associated with adverse childhood outcomes. Yet, despite infants’ greater developmental vulnerability, prospective data characterizing maltreatment throughout the first years of life remain scarce. We aimed to examine the distribution and trajectories of exposure to maltreatment across infancy and toddlerhood in two socioeconomically distinct Brazilian populations. 

Methods: We analyzed data on 681 children from two longitudinal studies. Maltreatment was assessed from infancy through toddlerhood using 3-5 repeated measures of the Conflict Tactics Scales: Parent-child Version and operationalized as cumulative exposure. Trajectories were estimated using monotonic integrated P-splines and group differences were assessed using likelihood ratio tests. 

Findings: Maltreatment was already reported at 3 months. Psychological aggression was the most prevalent subtype, reported in 26% of children by 3 months and in around 90% of both groups by 24 months. Corporal punishment was substantially more frequent in the socioeconomically vulnerable population (LR = 45·94, p < 0·002). At 24 months, more than 95% of all children had been ever exposed to at least one subtype maltreatment behaviour. Co-occurrence was more common than isolated exposure by 12 months (60·3% and 79·7% of exposed infants), a pattern that continued to increase by 24 months (81·3% and 92·8%). 

Interpretation: Maltreatment rapidly accumulates during the first childhood years across different socioeconomic contexts. While socioeconomic vulnerability was substantially associated with corporal punishment, the results suggest an important role of culture in caregiving practices overall. Preventive efforts should begin during pregnancy and address maltreatment as a continuum of practices.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how Bitcoin prices and volatility respond to the Russia-Ukraine war, distinguishing between attention to the conflict itself and attention to SWIFT-related sanctions. Using high-frequency Bitcoin data from Coinbase and Google Trends measures of global attention, we investigate the relationships between geopolitical attention and Bitcoin returns and realized volatility, including its jump and continuous components. We find that increased attention to the war is associated with lower Bitcoin returns and higher realized volatility, affecting both its continuous and jump components. In contrast, SWIFT-related attention is negatively associated with Bitcoin jump volatility, while its contemporaneous relationship with Bitcoin returns is statistically insignificant. Additional analysis reveals that lagged SWIFT-related attention positively predicts subsequent Bitcoin returns. These findings highlight the distinct relationships between different forms of geopolitical attention and Bitcoin market dynamics, consistent with Bitcoin’s dual role as a speculative asset and a potential alternative cross-border transaction mechanism.

detail.abstract: What happens when the American dream of homeownership becomes a corporate asset class? Institutional investor ownership of single‑family rentals (SFRs) reduces the number of homes available for individual purchase and drives up home values—a trend that is beneficial for existing homeowners, but detrimental for prospective buyers. Although the creation of new single‑family rental units has been lauded as a public good to fill the housing gap for those who cannot afford to purchase, it is perpetuating a cycle in which individuals lose out on the opportunity to build equity and intergenerational wealth. The topic of investor ownership of SFRs has received a flurry of attention from federal legislators and the executive branch under the Trump Administration. Title X of the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (ROAD to Housing Act, or the Act) bans institutional investors who own 350 or more single‑family homes from buying additional single‑family homes or duplexes. Because of the nature of property law, however, and because of the limited scope of the 350 threshold, the protections of this federal intervention should be augmented by state and local governments who may more carefully tailor their policies to local housing markets. This Article explores principles of federalism as applied to a corporate land ban, explaining the possible role of each level of government in passing and enforcing SFR restrictions.

detail.abstract:
Background: Accurate preoperative lymph node metastasis (LNM) assessment on computed tomography (CT) in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains challenging. The aim of this study is to develop and validate an artificial intelligence (AI) tool NODAL-MAP for preoperative LNM identification in ESCC using a multicenter dataset.

Methods: The NODAL-MAP was developed using a retrospective internal cohort of consecutive ESCC patients undergoing upfront radical esophagectomy at Sichuan Cancer Hospital (2009–2018), and externally validated across three independent cohorts. Regional lymph nodes (LNs) with nodal stations were automatically segmented on contrast-enhanced chest CT scans, with metastasis status manually annotated based on histopathology. NODAL-MAP’s diagnostic performance was primarily evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and its 95% confidence interval (CI), and further compared against four board-certified oncologists. Statistical significance was defined as a two-sided P < 0.05.

Findings: NODAL-MAP was developed using 2,631 LN masks (188 metastatic, 7.1%) from 815 ESCC patients, and externally validated on 4,314 LN masks from 657 patients. NODAL-MAP achieved an AUC of 0.92 (95% CI: 0.90, 0.94) for lesion-level LNM identification in the internal dataset under five-fold cross-validation with the most optimal sensitivity 0.85 and specificity 0.86, and AUCs of 0.89 (95% CI: 0.86, 0.92), 0.90 (95% CI: 0.86, 0.93), and 0.89 (95% CI: 0.86, 0.91) in the external test set 1, 2, and 3, respectively. For patient-level nodal staging (N0 vs N+), NODAL-MAP demonstrated an AUC of 0.86 (95% CI: 0.84, 0.89) in the internal dataset with the most optimal sensitivity 0.73 and specificity 0.85, and AUCs of 0.84 (95% CI: 0.79, 0.88), 0.85 (95% CI: 0.77, 0.92), and 0.81 (95% CI: 0.75, 0.86) in the external test set 1, 2, and 3, respectively. NODAL-MAP significantly outperformed the four experienced oncologists in LNM identification (AUC 0.91 vs 0.66–0.78, P < 0.05) and N-stage classification (AUC 0.83 vs 0.53–0.67, P < 0.05) in reader study.

Interpretation: AI-based NODAL-MAP model identifying LNM in ESCC accurately was successfully developed with rigorous validations. NODAL-MAP could serve as a valuable AI tool for the precise mapping of metastatic LNs in ESCC.

detail.abstract:
Background: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) increases cardiovascular and motor vehicle collision risk. Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) is first-line therapy, but its cardiovascular benefit depends on adherence. Hypoglossal nerve stimulation (HGNS) is an implantable option for CPAP-intolerant patients, yet its cost-effectiveness has not been assessed in Canada. We estimated the cost-effectiveness of HGNS versus CPAP versus no treatment for moderate-to-severe OSA from a Canadian provincial public-payer perspective. 

Methods: We built a six-state Markov cohort model (20-year horizon, 1-year cycles, 1·5% discounting, reported per CHEERS 2022) of Canadian adults aged 40–60 years (75% male) with moderate-to-severe OSA (apnea–hypopnea index ≥15 events per hour). HGNS was modelled in CPAP-intolerant patients. Event risks combined Canadian epidemiologic data with multiplicative hazard ratios. Costs are in 2024 Canadian dollars (CAD). The primary outcome was the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) per quality-adjusted life-year (QALY) gained, against a willingness-to-pay threshold of CAD$50,000 per QALY. Subgroup, one-way deterministic, and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were conducted. 

Findings: Over 20 years, HGNS accrued 16·48 QALYs ($187,646), CPAP 13·35 QALYs ($100,296), and no treatment 12·93 QALYs ($88,464). The ICER for HGNS versus CPAP was CAD$27,872 per QALY (incremental cost $87,349; incremental QALYs 3·13). Compared with CPAP, HGNS was projected to prevent 24 myocardial infarctions, 31 strokes, and 60 deaths per 1000 patients. HGNS was cost-effective versus CPAP in 61·8% of probabilistic iterations at CAD$50,000 per QALY and 74·8% at CAD$100,000 per QALY. The ICER exceeded CAD$50,000 per QALY when the HGNS well-state utility fell below 0·85, but remained cost-effective at CAD$30,652 per QALY with no mortality benefit. 

Interpretation: HGNS could be a cost-effective alternative to CPAP for CPAP-intolerant adults, supporting formal Canadian health technology assessment. This conclusion depends on the assumed HGNS utility advantage, which needs confirmation in Canadian cohorts.​

detail.abstract: When do risks become real to economic agents? Many environmental hazards are publicly known long before they cause damage, yet remain economically latent. We study how markets respond when a long-known environmental risk becomes highly salient before catastrophic losses occur, using a natural experiment from Italy where renewed seismic unrest heightened public attention without widespread destruction, fatalities, or formal risk reclassification. Sale prices fall in the most exposed ownership market, while rents rise as households adjust across tenure and space. High-frequency congestion tests show that responses to seismic signals weaken when unrelated events compete for attention, while complementary evidence illustrates the adjustment mechanisms. Salience is an important part of the process through which known environmental risk becomes decision-relevant and capitalized before that risk fully materializes.

detail.abstract: When the Federal Reserve shifted to an ample-reserves framework, many observers started to question the relevance of the fed funds market. With reserves ample or abundant and rates anchored by administered floors, interbank borrowing declined sharply, and the market appeared to serve mainly as an arbitrage venue for non-bank institutions.

detail.abstract: Popular music charts changed what they measure when streaming replaced sales. A purchase-based chart records acquisition, and a purchase extinguishes the demand it registers; a streaming chart records use, and every play counts anew. Demand that recurs on a fixed schedule for a fixed repertoire was therefore invisible to the sales-era instrument and fully visible to its successor. Using daily Spotify Top 200 charts for Germany (2017-2025) matched to audio features, and weekly chart data spanning 1977-2025, we show that seasonality in the acoustic character of charted music is a phenomenon of the streaming era: absent before 2015, growing steadily since, and dominated by Christmas. On December 24 streaming volume reached 4.6 times the annual daily mean in 2024, up from 2.9 in 2017, and the charts shift sharply toward high acousticness and low energy. The pattern is selective across twenty holidays: Easter, which shares Christmas's family character, produces no acoustic effect at all, while New Year's Eve moves the charts in the opposite direction. The December peak is carried by a fixed and aging catalog, but age is that catalog's property rather than its cause: on an ordinary day old recordings are less acoustic and more energetic than contemporary releases, so a shift in age composition alone would move December the wrong way. The December component of any series built from these charts therefore reflects the recirculation of a fixed historical catalog rather than contemporary listening, with direct consequences for the seasonal adjustment of music-based sentiment indicators.

detail.abstract: Workers care not only about pay and career opportunities but also about meaningful work and socially responsible employers. This heterogeneity matters for worker-firm matching, recruitment, and compensation, yet its preference-based origins remain poorly understood. In a two-wave study of a sample broadly representative of the Swiss adult population (N=1,031), we study whether social preferences provide a common account of life goals, job preferences, and occupational sorting. We structurally estimate two facets of social preferences: altruism in the advantageous and in the disadvantageous domain. We show that these two dimensions are negatively correlated, and that failing to account for both can substantially bias — in our applications, underestimate — the effects of social preferences. Social preferences predict respondents’ life goals, their preferred job attributes, and their willingness to work in the tobacco industry. In particular, higher altruism is associated with lower emphasis on wealth, financial security, career status, pay, and advancement, but greater emphasis on corporate social responsibility and meaningful work. It also predicts greater willingness to avoid working in the tobacco industry. Lastly, altruism when ahead is positively associated with employment in education, health, and social services. Thus, this paper highlights the importance of social preferences for explaining worker motivation and labor-market sorting.

detail.abstract: Professional forecasters' heterogeneous narratives about how inflation affects stock markets in 2023 rationalize their high disagreement regarding quantitative expectations for 12-month-ahead inflation and stock returns in December 2022. Professional forecasters causally update their return expectations in heterogeneous directions in response to information about the inflation outlook, depending on the narrative they entertain. Moreover, the narratives also affect their asset allocation in a hypothetical portfolio-choice experiment. Providing common signals does not necessarily lead to convergence of beliefs if agents subscribe to different narratives.

title: Optimal Taxation of Indistinguishable Activities
affiliations: University of Chicago - Law School, Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU) and Dalhousie University

detail.title: Optimal Taxation of Indistinguishable Activities
detail.abstract: Optimal tax policy frequently prescribes different tax treatments for activities that are difficult in practice for tax administrators to distinguish, such as expenditures undertaken for business versus personal purposes. We study the optimal design of income tax deductions for such expenditures under the assumption that a common deduction rate must be applied to both forms of the expenditure. The Pareto optimal common deduction turns on the relative compensated spending response for each margin, weighted by the income tax wedge. We also characterize the welfare gain from distinguishing between the two expenditure forms as a harmonic mean of the compensated responses. We illustrate both results with an application to air travel expenses.

title: Gender Differences in the Genetics of Skill Formation
affiliations: Aarhus University and Independent

detail.title: Gender Differences in the Genetics of Skill Formation
detail.abstract: This paper examines heterogeneity in the gender gap in early cognitive skills. While boys lag behind on average, we document both a socioeconomic and a genetic gradient, with disadvantaged boys falling substantially further behind comparable girls. Estimating a dynamic skill formation model, we show that the genetic gradient reflects boys’ greater sensitivity to their own endowments, while the socioeconomic gradient can be explained by genetic differences, higher returns to parental investment, and stronger skill self-productivity among boys. Differences in parental investments further amplify both the average gender gap and the overrepresentation of boys at both tails of the skill distribution.

detail.abstract: China’s export expansion increasingly challenges advanced-economy exporters in third markets. Using confidential German exporter data, we generalize the canonical China-shock instrument to multiple destinations, exploiting Chinese gains in products across similar markets. Within firms, export growth falls in destination-product markets where Chinese market shares rise, through weaker growth among continuing relationships and market exit. Growth in estimated quality and unit values also declines, while stronger quality, price, product, and destination advantages cushion losses. Market exit and weaker entry account for more than half of aggregate adjustment. Structural-gravity evidence attributes China’s gains mainly to quantity expansion and rising exporter-product competitiveness.
